record.title: Partial List Coloring Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $L$ be a list assignment, and let $\alpha_L(G)$ be the maximum number of vertices that can be properly $L$-colored. For a positive integer $t$, let $\alpha_t^\ell(G)$ be the minimum of $\alpha_L(G)$ over all $t$-assignments $L$ for $G$, and let $\chi_\ell(G)$ denote the list chromatic number of $G$. For an integer $t$, write $[\chi_\ell(G)]$ for the set of positive integers at most $\chi_\ell(G)$. **Partial List Coloring Conjecture.** For any graph $G$ and $t \in [\chi_\ell(G)]$, 
$$
\alpha_t^\ell(G) \geq \frac{t|V(G)|}{\chi_\ell(G)}.
$$
 While the conjecture is still open, weaker general lower bounds are known, including bounds in terms of the ordinary chromatic number and other estimates.
record.source_name: Hemanshu Kaul, Jeffrey A. Mudrock and Michael J. Pelsmajer, “Partial DP-Coloring”, arXiv:2003.02687 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02687

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2020).

record.title: Juhász's depth bound conjecture for taut foliations
record.statement:
Let $(M,\gamma)$ be a taut balanced sutured manifold with $H_2(M)=0$. The sutured Floer homology $SFH(M,\gamma)$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{Z}_2$, and let $k$ be such that

$$
\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(SFH(M,\gamma))<2^{k+1}.
$$

**Juhász's conjecture.** The sutured manifold $(M,\gamma)$ admits a taut foliation of depth at most $2k$.

This conjecture seeks a bound on the depth of the taut foliations whose existence was established by Gabai. It relates the complexity of sutured Floer homology to the minimum possible depth, and its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Zhenkun Li, “Instanton and the depth of taut foliations”, arXiv:2003.02891 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02891

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

record.title: The balanced-bipartite Cartesian-product Hamiltonicity conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with a path factor, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices. The Cartesian product $P_n\square G$ is **balanced bipartite** when its two bipartition classes have equal size. **The balanced-bipartite Cartesian-product Hamiltonicity conjecture.** If $n\geq 4\Delta(G)-2$ and $P_n\square G$ is balanced bipartite, then $P_n\square G$ is Hamiltonian. This conjecture proposes Hamiltonicity under the stated degree bound and balance condition; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Louis Kao and Chih-wen Weng, “The relation between Hamiltonian and 1-tough properties of the Cartesian product graphs”, arXiv:2003.03084 (2020).

record.title: Conjecture on the orientability order of the universal complex line bundle for EO-theory
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a formal group of height $n=(p-1)k$, and let $\mathbb{C}$ denote the complex line bundle appearing in the definition of the orientability order $\Theta$. **Orientability-order conjecture.**

$$
\Theta(\mathrm{EO}_{\Gamma},\mathbb{C})=p^k.
$$

This conjectures the exact value of the $\mathrm{EO}_{\Gamma}$-orientability order in the case that the height is divisible by $p-1$. Previously known results give non-sharp bounds in some cases, including height $p-1$ and at the prime $2$, so the asserted equality remains open here.
record.source_name: Prasit Bhattacharya and Hood Chatham, “On the EO-orientability of vector bundles”, arXiv:2003.03795 (2021).

record.title: The chain-is-best conjecture for poset saturation
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset with $k$ elements, let $C_k$ denote the chain on $k$ elements, and let ${\rm sat}(n,P)$ be the minimum size of a maximal $P$-free subposet of the Boolean lattice $B_n$.

**Chain-is-best conjecture.** For any $k$-element poset $P$, we have

$$
{\rm sat}(n,P)\le {\rm sat}(n,C_k).
$$

The conjecture asks whether the chain is the hardest $k$-element poset to saturate. The paper has already established the general upper bound ${\rm sat}(n,P)\le 2^{k-2}$, while the known lower bound for chains shows that exponential growth in $k$ is possible; the comparison with ${\rm sat}(n,C_k)$ remains open.
record.source_name: Balázs Keszegh, Nathan Lemons, Ryan R. Martin, Dömötör Pálvölgyi and Balázs Patkós, “Induced and non-induced poset saturation problems”, arXiv:2003.04282 (2022).

record.title: The boundedness conjecture for induced saturation under adjoining a maximum
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, and let $\dot P$ denote the poset obtained from $P$ by adjoining a largest element. Write ${\rm sat}^*(n,P)$ for the minimum size of a maximal induced $P$-free subposet of the Boolean lattice $B_n$.

**Adjoining-a-maximum conjecture.** The quantity ${\rm sat}^*(n,P)$ is bounded as a function of $n$ if and only if ${\rm sat}^*(n,\dot P)$ is bounded as a function of $n$.

The observation preceding the conjecture shows one implication at the level of saturating families when $P$ has no largest element, but the authors could verify neither direction in general. The equivalence is known only in special cases and remains open.

record.title: Circular-arc conjecture for minimizers of the Gamma-limit functional
record.statement:
Assume that $\mathcal{K}$ is not central. Let $M
ein\mathbb{N}$ be as in the symmetry condition, and let $(\Delta\theta)_{\min}$ be the minimum total angle compatible with $\mathcal{K}$. Let $v_I^*\in\overline{\mathcal{K}}$ be a minimizer of the Gamma-limit functional $\overline{\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}_0^\alpha}$. **Circular-arc conjecture.** If $(\Delta\theta)_{\min}/M<2\pi$, then the trajectory $v_I^*([0,T])$ is composed of circular arcs centered at the origin and passing through some rotation axes, which are swept with uniform motion. The conjecture predicts the structure of minimizers in the noncentral-cone case for $\alpha\in(1,2)$; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

record.title: The cost classification conjecture for skew-layered permutations
record.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a skew-layered permutation of size $n$, and let $\mathsf{cost}(\pi)$ denote its pop-stack sorting cost. Exclude $\mathsf{id}$ and $-\mathsf{id}$. **Skew-layered cost classification conjecture.** If $n$ is even, then

$$
\mathsf{cost}(\pi)=n-1.
$$

If $n$ is odd and the $(n+1)/2$-th position of $\pi$ is the central point of a run or of a fall of size at least $3$, then $\mathsf{cost}(\pi)=n-2$; otherwise, $\mathsf{cost}(\pi)=n-1$. This conjecture refines the preceding necessary condition for permutations of maximum cost and is based on the authors' computer experiments; a general characterization of all maximum-cost permutations remains open.
record.source_name: Andrei Asinowski, Cyril Banderier and Benjamin Hackl, “Flip-sort and combinatorial aspects of pop-stack sorting”, arXiv:2003.04912 (2021).

record.title: Ahmadi–Shparlinski's maximal angle rank conjecture for Jacobians
record.statement:
Let $J$ be an ordinary, geometrically simple Jacobian over a finite field. Its **angle rank** is the invariant referred to in the conjecture, and **maximal angle rank** means that this invariant takes its largest possible value.

**Ahmadi–Shparlinski's conjecture.** Every ordinary, geometrically simple Jacobian over a finite field has maximal angle rank.

The paper reports that this conjecture is false and gives two counterexamples in dimension $4$.
record.source_name: Taylor Dupuy, Kiran Kedlaya, David Roe and Christelle Vincent, “Counterexamples to a Conjecture of Ahmadi and Shparlinski”, arXiv:2003.05368 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: Compactly supported formulation of the sharp autocorrelation constant
record.statement:
Let $C_4$ be the smallest constant such that

$$
\min_{t\in[0,1]}\int_{\mathbb{R}}f(x)f(t+x)\,dx\leq C_4\|f\|_1^2
$$

for the function class specified in Theorem 4 of the source. The compactly supported formulation concerns functions $f\in L^1([-1/2,1/2])$. **Compact-support conjecture for $C_4$.**

$$
C_4=\sup_{f\in L^1([-1/2,1/2])}\inf_{t\in[0,1]}\frac{|f\star f(t)|}{\|f\|_1^2}.
$$

This conjecture would identify the best constant from the almost-compactly-supported problem with the supremum over compactly supported functions. The paper notes that an explicit compactly supported example gives a lower bound, while Theorem 4 only establishes a strict improvement over a previous upper bound; equality with the compact-support supremum remains open.
record.source_name: José Madrid and João P. G. Ramos, “On optimal autocorrelation inequalities on the real line”, arXiv:2003.06962 (2020).

record.title: Positive Lyapunov exponent conjecture for projective K3 automorphisms
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a projective $K3$ surface, let $T:X\to X$ be an automorphism with positive topological entropy $h>0$, and fix a Ricci-flat Kähler metric $\omega$. Define the largest Lyapunov exponent of the Lebesgue measure $\mathrm{dVol}$ by

$$
\Lambda=\int_X\left(\lim_{N\to+\infty}\frac{h}{2N}\log\|D_xT^N\|_\omega\right)\mathrm{dVol}(x).
$$

**Positive Lyapunov exponent conjecture.** One has $\Lambda>0$.

The exponent is known to be finite and nonnegative. Positivity is identified as a major outstanding problem; the source also notes that a dense $T$-orbit would already be interesting in this setting.
record.source_name: Valentino Tosatti, “Ricci-flat metrics and dynamics on K3 surfaces”, arXiv:2003.06976 (2020).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06976

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2020). “In this last section we briefly discuss a few open problems related to the dynamics of automorphisms of $K3$ surfaces that the author learned from S. Filip, see also Cantat's ICM paper for many other problems.”

record.title: Segre final-gap formula
record.statement:
Let $X=\sigma_{n,m}(\mathbb{P}^n\times\mathbb{P}^m)$, so that the relevant codimension is $nm$. Let $\mathfrak{L}_j(X)$ denote the $j$th secant index. **Segre final-gap conjecture.** One has

$$
\mathfrak{L}_{nm}(X)-\mathfrak{L}_{nm-1}(X)=\binom{n+m-2}{n-1}.
$$

Equivalently, the maximum finite reduced intersection with a linear subvariety of dimension $nm-1$ is

$$
\binom{n+m}{n}-\binom{n+m-2}{n-1}.
$$

This is presented as a consequence of the Segre secant-index conjecture and remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Grayson Jorgenson, “Secant indices of projective varieties”, arXiv:2003.08481 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.08481

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2020). “This is therefore also an implication of the EGH-conjecture, so any counterexample to it would also suffice to disprove the EGH-conjecture.”

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for the convexity-deficit distribution of benzenoids
record.statement:
Let $h\geq 0$, and let $F(h,k)$ denote the number of benzenoids on $h$ hexagons having convexity deficit equal to $k$. Let $\operatorname{mcd}(h)$ be the maximum convexity deficit among benzenoids on $h$ hexagons. **Unimodality conjecture.** The sequence

$$
F(h,0), F(h,1), F(h,2), \ldots, F(h,\operatorname{mcd}(h))
$$

is unimodal. This conjecture concerns the distribution of benzenoids by convexity deficit; the paper reports the pattern from computed data but does not establish it in general.
record.source_name: Nino Bašić, Sarah Berkemer, Jörg Fallmann, Patrick W. Fowler, Thomas Gatter, Tomaž Pisanski, Nancy Retzlaff, Peter F. Stadler and Sara S. Zemljič, “Convexity deficit of benzenoids”, arXiv:2003.09716 (2020).

record.title: The critical-diagonal conjecture for phase transition in the area-interaction model
record.statement:
Let $z\geq 0$ be the activity and let $\beta\geq 0$ be the inverse temperature of the area-interaction model. Phase transition means non-uniqueness of the area-interaction measures for these parameters. **Critical-diagonal conjecture.** There exists $0<\beta_c<\infty$ such that phase transition occurs if and only if

$$
z=\beta>\beta_c.
$$

The conjecture describes the still-unresolved phase diagram: existing results establish substantial bounds and an almost complete picture, but do not determine the full uniqueness/non-uniqueness region.
record.source_name: Pierre Houdebert, “Numerical study for the phase transition of the area-interaction model”, arXiv:2003.10754 (2020).

record.title: The one-dimensional positive sign uncertainty conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{A}_+(1)$ denote the optimal constant for the one-dimensional positive sign uncertainty principle, and let

$$
\varphi:=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}2
$$

be the golden ratio.

**Positive sign uncertainty conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{A}_+(1)=(2\varphi)^{-\tfrac12}.
$$

The value is supported by numerical evidence from the discrete Fourier-transform problem and would determine the one-dimensional positive sign uncertainty constant exactly. The source presents it as conjectural.
record.source_name: Felipe Gonçalves, Diogo Oliveira e Silva and João P. G. Ramos, “New Sign Uncertainty Principles”, arXiv:2003.10771 (2023).

record.title: The minimum codegree threshold conjecture for two tight paths in 3-graphs
record.statement: Let $H$ be an $n$-vertex $3$-graph, and let $[?]$ denote its minimum codegree, the minimum number of common neighbours over all pairs of vertices. A collection of tight paths is **vertex-disjoint** if their vertex sets are pairwise disjoint, and it **covers** $V(H)$ if the union of their vertex sets is $V(H)$. **Minimum codegree threshold conjecture.** The minimum codegree assumption in the theorem guaranteeing two vertex-disjoint tight paths whose union covers $V(H)$ can be weakened to $n/3$; equivalently, minimum codegree at least $n/3$ should guarantee such a cover. This would make $n/3$ the asymptotically sharp threshold, since the stated three-part construction requires three tight paths.
record.source_name: Jie Han, “Cover 3-uniform hypergraphs by vertex-disjoint tight paths”, arXiv:2003.11686 (2022).

record.title: Chen's polymorphism dichotomy conjecture for the surjective constraint satisfaction problem
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite domain, let $\Gamma$ be a constraint language on $A$, and let $\operatorname{SCSP}(\Gamma)$ denote the surjective constraint satisfaction problem over $\Gamma$. An operation on $A$ is **idempotent** if $f(x,x,\ldots,x)=x$, and a weak near-unanimity operation is an operation satisfying

$$
f(y,x,\ldots,x)=f(x,y,x,\ldots,x)=\cdots=f(x,x,\ldots,x,y)
$$

for all $x,y\in A$; a polymorphism of $\Gamma$ preserves every relation in $\Gamma$. **Chen's polymorphism conjecture.** For any constraint language $\Gamma$, the problem $\operatorname{SCSP}(\Gamma)$ is solvable in polynomial time if there exists an idempotent WNU polymorphism of $\Gamma$; $\operatorname{SCSP}(\Gamma)$ is $NP$-complete otherwise. This is the polymorphism formulation of the preceding conjecture. The source's status evidence says the related conjectures hold for a two-element domain, while the paper's counterexample refutes the general SCSP characterization.
record.source_name: Dmitriy Zhuk, “No-Rainbow Problem and the Surjective Constraint Satisfaction Problem”, arXiv:2003.11764 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.11764

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2020). “In 2017 this conjecture was resolved independently by Andrei Bulatov and Dmitriy Zhuk .”

record.title: Xiao–Katona–Xiao–Zamora conjecture on the Turán number of squared paths
record.statement:
Denote by $P_k$ the path on $k$ vertices. Its square, $P_k^2$, is obtained by joining every pair of vertices whose distance in $P_k$ is less than $2$. Let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $H$.

**Xiao–Katona–Xiao–Zamora conjecture.** For the square of the path $P_k$, one has

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,P_k^2)\leq \max\left\{\frac{n_0\left(\left\lfloor\frac{2k}{3}\right\rfloor-2\right)}{2}+n_0n_1:n_0+n_1=n\right\}.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is settled, in a stronger form, by its characterization of the extremal graphs of powers of paths using a theorem of Simonovits.
record.source_name: Long-Tu Yuan, “Extremal graphs of the k-th power of paths”, arXiv:2003.12701 (2020).

record.title: The 1-2-3 Conjecture for vertex-colouring edge weightings
record.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph with at least two edges. A **$3$-weighting** of $G$ is a mapping $\omega:E\to\{1,2,3\}$, and it is **vertex-colouring** if the weighted degree $s_\omega(v)=\sum_{e\in E(v)}\omega(e)$ gives distinct values to the endpoints of every edge. **1-2-3 Conjecture.** Every connected graph with at least two edges admits a vertex-colouring $3$-weighting. This is the central 1-2-3 Conjecture, introduced by Karoński, Łuczak and Thomason. The paper proves the conjecture for graphs whose minimum degree is sufficiently large relative to the logarithm of their maximum degree, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Jakub Przybyło, “The 1-2-3 Conjecture holds for graphs with large enough minimum degree”, arXiv:2003.13139 (2020).

record.title: Upper edge-connectivity bound for the rainbow disconnection number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. The **upper edge-connectivity** $\lambda^+(G)$ is the maximum local edge-connectivity of $G$, and $\operatorname{rd}(G)$ denotes the rainbow disconnection number of $G$.

**Rainbow disconnection bound.** The conjecture states

$$
\lambda^+(G)\leq \operatorname{rd}(G)\leq \lambda^+(G)+1.
$$

This conjecture extends the bound known for connected regular graphs, complete multipartite graphs, and grid graphs. The paper proves it for many classes of graphs, but the general case is presented as open.
record.source_name: Xuqing Bai, Zhong Huang and Xueliang Li, “Bounds for the rainbow disconnection number of graphs”, arXiv:2003.13237 (2020).

record.title: Generic two-hot-spots conjecture for quantum graphs
record.statement:
Let $amma$ be a metric graph satisfying the standing assumptions of the paper. Write $mu_2(amma)$ for its second eigenvalue, and let $M$ be the set of global minima and maxima of corresponding second eigenfunctions.

**Generic two-hot-spots conjecture.** Generically, $mu_2(amma)$ is simple and the corresponding eigenfunction has exactly one minimum and one maximum, so that $|M|=2$.

The paper has results showing that this behaviour can be obtained after small modifications, but the generic assertion remains conjectural in the supplied text.

record.title: Hilton's Overfull Conjecture for dense graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$, maximum degree $\Delta$, chromatic index $\chi'(G)$, and fractional chromatic index $\chi'_f(G)$. **Hilton's Overfull Conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta>\frac{1}{3}|V(G)|,
$$

then

$$
\chi'(G)=\lceil \chi'_f(G)\rceil.
$$

The conjecture predicts exact rounding of the fractional chromatic index for graphs whose maximum degree exceeds one third of their order. It remains wide open.
record.source_name: Yan Cao, Guantao Chen, Guangming Jing and Songling Shan, “Proof of the Core Conjecture of Hilton and Zhao”, arXiv:2004.00734 (2020).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.00734

record.title: HZ-graph classification equivalent to the Core Conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be an **HZ-graph**, meaning a connected Class 2 graph with $\Delta(G_\Delta)\le2$, and let $P^*$ be the Petersen graph with one vertex removed. Let $\mathcal{O}_\Delta$ be the graph class defined in the paper. **HZ-graph classification conjecture.** If $G$ is an HZ-graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, then either $G\in\mathcal{O}_\Delta$, or $\Delta=2$ and $G$ is an odd cycle, or $\Delta=3$ and $G=P^*$. This is presented as an equivalent reformulation of the Core Conjecture and is therefore solved together with it.

record.title: Conjecture on the growth of two-colorings avoiding monochromatic even cycles
record.statement:
Let $f_k(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a $k$-edge-coloring of a graph on $n$ vertices that contains no monochromatic copy of $H$. For an integer $
\ell\geqslant 3$, consider the even cycle $C_{2\ell}$. **The conjecture.**

$$
f_{2}(n,C_{2\ell})=\Omega(n^{2-\frac{2}{\ell}}).
$$

This predicts a polynomial lower bound for the extremal function associated with two-colorings avoiding monochromatic copies of longer even cycles, extending the paper's investigation of the case $C_4$. The conjecture is presented as an open direction for future work.
record.source_name: Zixiang Xu, Tao Zhang, Yifan Jing and Gennian Ge, “Color isomorphic even cycles and a related Ramsey problem”, arXiv:2004.01932 (2020).

record.title: The Borel Dilworth conjecture
record.statement: Let $P=(V,\preceq)$ be a Borel poset, meaning that $V$ is a standard Borel space and the comparability relation is a Borel subset of $V\times V$. Its **width** is the maximum size of an antichain. **Borel Dilworth conjecture.** Every Borel poset $P$ of finite width $k$ is decomposable into $k$ Borel chains. This is the Borel analogue of Dilworth's theorem for finite posets; the paper proves the assertion only in special cases, so the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Bartłomiej Bosek, Jarosław Grytczuk and Zbigniew Lonc, “Dilworth's Theorem for Borel Posets”, arXiv:2004.02162 (2020).

record.title: The Borel dual Dilworth conjecture
record.statement: Let $P=(V,\preceq)$ be a Borel poset. Its **height** is the largest size of a chain in $P$, and an antichain is a set of pairwise incomparable elements. **Borel dual Dilworth conjecture.** Every Borel poset $P$ of finite height $h$ is decomposable into $h$ Borel antichains. This is the dual Borel analogue of Dilworth's theorem. The paper presents the statement as a conjectural extension; its general validity is not established there.

record.title: A strengthened Gerzon bound for spherical even-distance sets
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$ be a positive integer and let $s>0$ be an even integer. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq \mathbb S^{n-1}$ denote a spherical $s$-distance set with inner products $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ satisfying

$$
t_1+\ldots+t_s\geq 0.
$$

**Strengthened Gerzon bound.** Then

$$
|\mathcal S|\leq {n+s-1\choose s}.
$$

This is presented as a natural strengthening of the paper's preceding theorem. The claim concerns the maximum size of spherical distance sets under the additional nonnegative-sum condition on their inner products; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: Gábor Hegedüs, “A new proof of a generalization of Gerzon's bound”, arXiv:2004.02240 (2020).

record.title: Cube-section affine-cube extremality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n>k\geq 1$, let $\Box^n=[-1,1]^n$, and let $H$ be a $k$-dimensional linear subspace. Write $C_{\Box}(n,k)2^k$ for the maximum volume among sections $\Box^n\cap H$ that are affine cubes. **Cube-section affine-cube extremality conjecture.** The maximal volume of a section of the cube $\Box^n$ by a $k$-dimensional linear subspace $H$ is attained on subspaces for which the section is an affine cube; equivalently,

$$
\operatorname{vol}_{k}(\Box^n\cap H)\leq C_{\Box}(n,k)\operatorname{vol}_{k}\Box^k.
$$

This conjecture gives the proposed sharp upper bound in the cases where Ball's general upper bounds are not known to be tight, namely when $k$ does not divide $n$ and $2k<n$.
record.source_name: Grigory Ivanov and Igor Tsiutsiurupa, “On the volume of sections of the cube”, arXiv:2004.02674 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: Sturmfels–Uhler polynomiality conjecture for the maximum likelihood degree
record.statement: Let $V$ be a vector space, let $\boldsymbol{S}^2V$ denote the space of symmetric matrices on $V$, and let $c6(n,a)$ be the maximum likelihood degree associated with symmetric matrices of size $n$ and a general $a$-dimensional linear subspace. Sturmfels and Uhler suggest that, for fixed $a$, this invariant is polynomial in $n$. **Sturmfels\Uhler's polynomiality conjecture.** For fixed $a$ the function $c6(n,a)$ is a polynomial in $n$ of degree $a-1$. The theorem preceding the conjecture establishes the formula in several low-dimensional cases and gives all values for $n\leq 6$; the conjecture is presented as an extrapolation from these known values and remains unresolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Bethe quantum-number conjecture for the maximal six-vertex-model eigenvalue
record.statement:
Let $n$ be the fixed number of Bethe roots, let $H$ be the parameter in the transfer matrix, and let $I_j$ denote the corresponding Bethe quantum numbers. **Bethe quantum-number conjecture.** When the inhomogeneities and $H$ are sufficiently small, or when the system is homogeneous, the maximal eigenvalue corresponds to solutions of the Bethe equations with

$$
I_j=\frac{n+1-2j}{2},\qquad j=1,\ldots,n.
$$

This conjecture identifies the Bethe state describing the largest eigenvalue in the fixed-$n$ subspace. It has a long history in the Bethe-ansatz analysis of the Heisenberg XXZ chain and the six-vertex model, and is used to characterize the ground state and compute the thermodynamic free energy; the stated finite-$N$ claim remains presented as a conjecture here.

record.title: Mori–Reid–Tian conjecture on disjoint positive-genus curves on complex surfaces
record.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth complex surface with $b_1(X)=0$ and $b_2(X)>1$. Suppose that $D_i$ are smooth, pairwise disjoint complex curves on $X$, each of positive genus $g_i>0$, and that their homology classes span $H_2(X,\mathbb{Q})$. **Mori–Reid–Tian conjecture.** No such smooth complex surface $X$ exists. This conjecture would rule out the complex-surface configuration needed to construct a semi-regular Sasakian structure on the associated Seifert bundle, and is relevant to the distinction between semi-regular K-contact and Sasakian structures. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: The maximum-scattered-subspace count conjecture for the family $U_b$
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let

$$
\Gamma:=\{\operatorname{N}_{q^6/q^3}(b): U_b \text{ is maximum scattered}\},
$$

where

$$
U_b=\{(x,bx^q+x^{q^4}):x\in\mathbb{F}_{q^6}\}.
$$

**The maximum-scattered-subspace count conjecture.**

$$
|\Gamma|=\left\lfloor\frac{(q^2+q+1)(q-2)}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The quantity $|\Gamma|$ counts pairwise non-$\operatorname{GL}(2,q^6)$-equivalent maximum scattered subspaces of the form $U_b$. The authors state this after proving that $\Gamma$ is nonempty; the conjecture concerns how large the resulting family of inequivalent subspaces is.

record.title: Perfect-matching index four characterization of shortest cycle covers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. Write $scc(G)$ for the minimum total length of a cycle cover, and let $\chi'_{e}(G)$ denote the edge-chromatic number of $G$. **Perfect-matching index four shortest-cycle-cover conjecture.**

$$
scc(G)=\frac{4}{3}\lvert E(G)\rvert\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \chi'_{e}(G)\leq 4.
$$

The source proposes this equivalence and shows that it is implied by the shortest four-cycle-cover conjecture. It remains open.

record.title: Bounded critical number conjecture for $I_s$-free triangle-free matroids
record.statement:
Let $s\geq 4$. An $I_s$-free matroid is a binary matroid with no restriction isomorphic to the $s$-dimensional projective geometry $I_s$, and a triangle-free matroid has no three-element circuit. The critical number of a matroid $M=(E,G)$ is

$$
\chi(M)=\dim(G)-\omega(M^c),
$$

where $M^c$ is the complementary matroid and $\omega(M)$ is the dimension of a largest subgeometry of $M$ contained in $E$.

**Bounded critical number conjecture.** For any $s\geq 4$, the class of $I_s$-free and triangle-free matroids has bounded critical number.

The conjecture asks for a bound on the critical numbers depending only on $s$, not on the dimension of the matroids. The source notes that the result proved there settles the case $s=4$; the cases $s>4$ remain open in the supplied context.

record.title: The Graovac-Ghorbani index upper-bound conjecture for bicyclic graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}'_n$ be the family of all bicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices, and let $G\in\mathcal{B}'_n$ have order $n\geq 8$. The Graovac-Ghorbani atom-bond connectivity index is denoted by $ABC_{GG}(G)$. Let $H$ be the graph obtained by adding $n-4$ pendant vertices to one degree-$3$ vertex of $K_4$ with one edge removed. **Upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
ABC_{GG}(G)\leq (n-4)\sqrt{\frac{n-2}{n-1}}+\sqrt{\frac{n-4}{n-3}}+2\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{n-2}}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. Computational experiments suggest that this graph gives the maximum of the index among all bicyclic graphs for $n\geq 8$.

record.title: Packing-minima transference conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $K_c=\frac12(K-K)$ be its central symmetral, and let $\Lambda$ be a lattice in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Write $[K_c]^\star$ and $[\Lambda]^\star$ for the polar body and dual lattice, respectively, and let $\rho_i(K,\Lambda)$ denote the $i$th packing minimum.

**Packing-minima transference conjecture.** For $1\leq j\leq n$,

$$
\rho_j(K,\Lambda)\,\rho_{n-j+1}([K_c]^\star,[\Lambda]^\star)\geq\frac12.
$$

This is proposed as a complete packing-minima analogue of the lower bound in Banaszczyk's transference inequality. The statement is open in the source.

record.title: Quillen's conjecture on the poset of elementary abelian p-subgroups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p$ be a prime dividing $|G|$. Let ${\mathcal{A}}_p(G)$ be the poset of non-trivial elementary abelian $p$-subgroups of $G$, ordered by inclusion, and let $|{\mathcal{A}}_p(G)|$ denote its geometric realization. Let $O_p(G)$ be the largest normal $p$-subgroup of $G$. **Quillen's conjecture.** If $|{\mathcal{A}}_p(G)|$ is contractible, then $O_p(G)\neq 1$. This is Quillen's conjecture relating the topology of the poset of elementary abelian $p$-subgroups to the existence of a nontrivial normal $p$-subgroup. The paper proves a strong version of the conjecture for most finite classical groups in non-defining characteristic, but the stated implication is not resolved in full generality here.

record.title: Odd-uniformity Erdős–Gallai threshold conjecture for link graphs
record.statement:
Let $1\leqslant d\leqslant k-2$, and set $\ell=k-d$. Let $\mathrm{eg}(\ell)$ be the smallest edge-density threshold such that every sufficiently large $\ell$-uniform hypergraph above that density contains a tightly connected subgraph with a fractional matching of density greater than $1/(\ell+1)$ and edge density greater than $1/2$.

**Odd-uniformity link-graph conjecture.** When $k-d$ is odd, $\mathrm{eg}(k-d)$ is attained by the $(k-d)$-uniform link graphs of the Han–Zhao construction.

The link graphs give the lower bounds $\mathrm{eg}(1)\geqslant1/2$ and $\mathrm{eg}(3)\geqslant5/8$. The source says the coincidence is believed but provides no proof of the asserted attainment.

record.title: The asymptotic gonality-point equality conjecture for binary curves
record.statement:
Let $N_2(g,\gamma)$ denote the maximum number of $\b5\mathbb{F}_2$-rational points on a curve of genus $g$ and gonality $\gamma$. For a curve over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with a degree-$\gamma$ morphism to $\mathbb{P}^1$, one has $\#C(\mathbb{F}_2)\leq 3\gamma$.

**Gonality-point equality conjecture.** Fix $\gamma\geq 2$. For $g$ sufficiently large,

$$
N_2(g,\gamma)=3\gamma.
$$

The conjecture asserts that, after the low-genus obstructions disappear, the elementary gonality-point upper bound is attained. The supplied text does not indicate whether this has been resolved.

record.title: The character sum cancellation conjecture for rough integers
record.statement:
Let $q$ be large and let $\chi$ be a non-principal character modulo $q$. For real numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfying

$$
\log q\leq y\leq x,
$$

and writing $P(n)$ for the largest prime factor of $n$ and $e(\alpha)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$, **the rough character sum conjecture.**

$$
\max_{\alpha\in[0,1]}\left|\sum_{\substack{n\leq x\\P(n)>y}}\frac{\chi(n)}{n}e(\alpha n)\right|\ll 1.
$$

If true, this would make the inequalities in the paper's main lower bounds equalities, supporting the claim that those results are best possible; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
